model_answer:
Netflix's average monthly revenue per paying membership (ARM) rose from **$10.82 in 2019 to $11.70 in 2024**. That is an increase of about **8.1%**, or roughly 1.6% a year. Most of the gain came in 2020–2021, and ARM has been nearly flat since.

| Year | ARM (monthly, global) | Change vs. prior year |
|---|---|---|
| 2019 | $10.82 | +5% |
| 2020 | $10.91 | ~+1% |
| 2021 | $11.67 | ~+7% |
| 2022 | $11.76 | +1% |
| 2023 | $11.64 | ~−1% |
| 2024 | $11.70 | ~+1% |

Figures are from Netflix's 10-K filings for FY2019, FY2022 and FY2024. I worked out the year-over-year changes myself from those figures.

**What drove the changes**
- **2019:** Netflix attributed the 5% rise to price changes and a shift toward higher-priced plans. Unfavorable foreign exchange partly offset it.
- **2021:** The jump reflects price increases across many markets.
- **2022:** ARM grew only 1%. Netflix said price changes were partly offset by a stronger U.S. dollar.
- **2022–2024:** ARM was essentially flat, even though paid memberships kept growing quickly. Average paying memberships were 222.9 million in 2022 and 277.7 million in 2024. Growth in lower-priced regions such as Asia-Pacific pulled the global average down. APAC ARM was $7.64 in 2023, against $9.56 in 2021. Price increases and foreign exchange moves also affected the average.

**Caveats**
- ARM is a global average, so it hides big regional gaps. In the 2019 filings, U.S. ARM was in the $12–13 range and international was about $10.
- Netflix stopped reporting quarterly membership counts and ARM starting in 2025. 2024 is therefore the last full year of this data.
- One site, Backlinko, lists the 2019–2024 increase as 35.89%. That doesn't match the filings, which give about 8%.
judge_reason: All yearly ARM figures and the flat 2022–24 trend are correct, but the answer omits the ~2.8% annual 2019–22 growth and the ad-plan explanation.
